chapter: Carnegie Hall and the touring years
title: Touring with Little Bo's band and singer Sheila Guys
summary: In Kansas City he met singer Sheila Guys and toured the Midwest and a boat date with the young band.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: So's we's in Kansas...went back to Kansas City, an' I was in a hotel--the Lincoln Hotel, there. We sittin' around and havin' a few drinks with a bunch of my old-time friends. They sent me a girl singer called Sheila Guys (?). I had never seen her before. So they called me on the phone, tol' me there was a lady downstairs wantsta sing with the band and for me to come downstairs.

So I got up off the bed and went downstairs and met Sheila Guys (?). She was a young lady...somethin'...she wasn't too much older than the boys...the young boys I was workin' with. So we had a good time with them. So we got along real sporty. She took...she took up with the band...all the young kids in the band were crazy about her.

So we toured all over. [ ] Cleveland, Ohio...Detroit, Michigan. We used to play ever'where... went ever' place. First time I was ever on a boat, I was on a boat with the band. We were travellin' up around...lessee, where were we now? We's up in Michigan some place, and we worked with...we had to travel

on a boat to get to the next date. They had a band on the boat so all the kids sat in on the band. We had a jam session. Sheila Guys (?) sung. I sung. An' the people gettin' paid for it, they sung. We had a ball. So I toured with them about two...three years all over the country. I ain't never been down South. I didn't know much about it, so that was my first shot down South. So we done all right down there. And then I met a lot of people down in Texas. I went over to Mississippi ...Tennessee...jus' all over the South.
